mcat_description.short: Tin Shed is a prefabricated or site-fabricated roofed structure built using corrugated or colour-coated GI/steel sheets on a mild steel pipe or angle frame, sold as a complete erected structure or as a supply-and-install service.
mcat_description.long: In the Indian market, a Tin Shed refers to a light-gauge steel sheet structure comprising an MS hollow-section or angle-iron frame with corrugated GI, colour-coated, or Galvalume roofing sheets, typically erected on-site by fabricators. Structures range from small residential terrace covers and parking sheds to large industrial factory and warehouse sheds spanning 12 to 50+ feet. Sheet thickness typically runs 0.45–0.60 mm for standard roofing, with frame members using APL Apollo or TATA MS hollow sections in 18-gauge; insulated variants use PUF or sandwich panels for heat protection. The product is quoted and sold per square foot of covered area, inclusive of material and labour in most Indian B2B transactions.

market_context: In the Indian B2B market, 'Tin Shed' (Hindi: टीन शेड / teen shed) refers to a prefabricated or site-fabricated structure using corrugated GI, colour-coated (PPGI/PPGL), or Galvalume steel sheets on a mild steel hollow-section frame — the dominant commercial form confirmed across multiple fabricator and manufacturer sources. The governing BIS standard for the base sheet material is IS 277:2003 (Galvanized Steel Sheets, Plain and Corrugated), with standard roofing sheet thickness of 0.45–0.60 mm and zinc coating of 80–275 GSM. Frame members are typically APL Apollo or TATA MS hollow sections (18-gauge), with C/Z purlins for larger spans. Key product variants include plain GI corrugated sheds (lowest cost, most common for agricultural/temporary use), colour-coated steel sheds (PPGI, dominant for industrial and commercial use), Galvalume sheds (superior corrosion resistance, coastal/humid climates), and insulated sandwich panel sheds (PUF/EPS core, for heat-sensitive industrial applications). The market is highly fragmented with local fabricators dominating; major steel brands (Jindal, JSW, TATA, APL Apollo) supply the raw sheet and frame material. Buyers search primarily by span dimension (12 ft, 15 ft, 20 ft) and quote per sq ft of covered area. 'Teen shade' and 'tin shade' are common phonetic misspellings used interchangeably by buyers in search queries.
